analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches and BASE/HEAD source. provider-release-cache.yml:73–76 selects qualification toolchains for PR warms and release toolchains otherwise; runner routing, read-only permissions and credential-free checkout remain unchanged. provider-signing-validation.yml:57–60,136–139 replaces inline SDK 27.0 checks with the reviewed tooling checkout's release selector; :89–93 delegates native build-system and SDK arguments to its Swift wrapper. Separate unsigned-build/signing jobs, same-run artifact retrieval, source/version checks, hardened signing, entitlement verification, notarization and secret cleanup remain unchanged. release-provider.yml:112–114 sets release mode globally and :1444 changes the compatibility artifact's required SDK to 27.2 while preserving commit and bundle-hash checks.
No concrete regression is established in these workflow changes. Relevant contracts are signed build identity/qualification (A-011, A-017, T-054), runtime signing protections (TB-003, T-013) and availability (A-018); no direct inference encryption, authorization, billing or plaintext handling change is visible. Material integration questions remain: inspect scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh and its wrapper to verify fail-closed release SDK selection and persistence into later steps, especially the signing job before credential import; inspect the provider-release-build action/cache implementation to verify qualification SDK objects cannot be reused as release objects without toolchain identity checks. These implementations are outside this batch, so neither missing checks nor safe behavior can be inferred. The release-provider workflow is supplied only as bounded hunks; integration must reconcile its other selector callers and artifact identity generation.
